_comment: Declarative manifest of INSTALLABLE (dynamic) vessels — the single source of truth for vessel-ctl.sh install/uninstall. Built-in vessels are baked into the image; this file is for vessels added/removed at runtime (federation, future). Each vessel: name (== systemd unit name), workdir (run dir; supports $REPO_ROOT), exec (bun entrypoint, relative to workdir), env (STATIC literal Environment= lines), secrets (keys from secrets.env.sh that must be in /etc/substrate/env — supplied to the unit via EnvironmentFile, NOT Environment=), restart, health_port (for /health + self-recovery), self_recovery (add to self-recovery-tick VESSELS), post_install (optional shell run after start, e.g. capture a dynamic relay multiaddr into /etc/substrate/env).

vessels.name: federation-relay
vessels.description: Public libp2p Circuit Relay v2 — the from-anywhere reachability anchor.
vessels.post_install: for i in $(seq 1 20); do m=$(grep -m1 'RELAY_MULTIADDR=' /workspace/fed-relay.log 2>/dev/null | sed 's/RELAY_MULTIADDR=//'); [ -n "$m" ] && { grep -v '^RELAY_MULTIADDR=' /etc/substrate/env > /etc/substrate/env.tmp && mv /etc/substrate/env.tmp /etc/substrate/env; echo "RELAY_MULTIADDR=$m" >> /etc/substrate/env; echo "captured RELAY_MULTIADDR=$m"; break; }; sleep 1; done

vessels.name: federation-transport-vessel
vessels.description: libp2p reachability + cross-substrate resolve-over-http + /health sensing surface.
